prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1381; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Evidence goes against the account: a nearby camera shows no collision at that place and time.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reports a sideswipe while changing lanes and states that the other vehicle struck the driver's side as they merged. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has given a recorded statement.

Entry 2: Policy confirms the driver is listed as a named insured and the vehicle is covered under the policy in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene. Claimant reports neck and back pain beginning shortly after the impact.

Entry 4: Photos of the vehicle show dents on the passenger side, at a lower height than the contact point described by the claimant. The damage pattern does not clearly line up with the account given so far.

Entry 5: Reviewed a nearby business camera covering the stretch of road. The footage shows no contact between vehicles at the location and time reported.

Entry 6: In a follow-up call, claimant now says the other car came from the opposite direction and that two passengers were present. The first statement described a single occupant and a different direction of travel.

Entry 7: Requested prior claims history for the vehicle and found no earlier damage recorded. Claimant also has no known prior injury to the neck or back on file.

Entry 8: Claimant was seen at an urgent care clinic and then referred to physical therapy. Clinic notes describe muscle strain consistent with a side impact of this kind.

Entry 9: Physical therapy notes show steady improvement over several weeks, with sessions becoming less frequent as range of motion returned. Treatment appears to have followed a normal course for this type of injury.

Entry 10: Re-interviewed the claimant about the camera footage and the discrepancies in the earlier statements. Claimant said the recollection of direction and passengers may have been mixed up due to stress after the event.

Entry 11: Sent the vehicle damage findings and the footage summary to the damage review unit for an independent assessment. Awaiting their opinion on whether the damage matches the reported impact.

Entry 12: Current status: injury plausible for this type of crash, treatment tapered as expected, and coverage confirmed. Claim remains open pending the damage review and a decision on the discrepancies in the camera evidence and the claimant's statements.
